- Google's extensive data collection on searches and interactions is a primary advantage for personalization but a point of contention for privacy advocates.

- The case follows a recent agreement where Google pays Canadian media $73.5 million annually for content use.

selected_passages.title: raw:sources/Is_Google_Search_better_than_the_rest_And_is_that_fair
selected_passages.text: For the US, which has to prove that Google somehow broke the law to achieve the status quo, this legal case could be an uphill battle. But for the rest of us, it offers a rare opportunity for some insight into what the tech giant does with its enormous market share. Is it still focused on being the best? Or, as has been alleged, does it use its ubiquity to squeeze us for money even at the expense of product quality? How ‘organic’ are Google’s results? This month, Wired posted an opinion article by lawyer and privacy advocate Megan Gray, which alleged that Google had accidentally revealed during the trial that it manipulates people’s search queries for maximum ad revenue. The example given was replacing a search for “children’s clothing” with “NIKOLAI-brand kidswear”. Loading Google rejected this in very strong terms, saying the piece was misleading and inaccurate while denying ever altering search terms. Wired removed the article for not meeting its standards, but the degree to which it was shared on social media and boosted in write-ups at other outlets shows just how willing people are to accept foul play on Google’s part. A suspicion of privacy invasion and inappropriate data handling follows the company at all times.

selected_passages.text:
- The lawsuit was filed in the U.S. District Court in D.C.
- Helena World Chronicle owns two weekly newspapers in Arkansas.
- Google's Search Generative Experience (SGE) is cited as worsening the problem.
- Google's Bard AI chatbot is cited as worsening the problem.
- The Knowledge Graph was launched in May 2012.
- By 2020, the Knowledge Graph contained 500 billion facts about 5 billion entities.
- Google drives nearly 40% of The Atlantic's traffic.
- The Atlantic modeled that AI would answer 75% of queries without a click-through.
- Publishers believe they will lose 20-40% of website traffic from Google's AI rollout.
- Axel Springer licensed news to OpenAI for AI model training.
- GoogleBot is the crawler used for both general search and SGE.
- Google paid $73.5 million (100 million Canadian dollars) to Canadian news organizations.
- Meta began blocking news in Canada in August.
- The U.S. Justice Department filed a separate antitrust suit against Google.
- The 2020 Justice Department suit was over search and search advertising.
- Epic Games won a recent lawsuit against Google over app store antitrust issues.
- Google links people to publisher websites more than 24 billion times monthly.
- News and Media sites were the third largest category of AI training data.
- The law firm handling the case is Hausfeld.
